transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-18
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 47 minutes (recording may have small gaps)
Attendees: Alex Ortega (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Asterial - Dir Data), Riley Santos (Asterial - ML Eng), Dana Kim (Asterial - Security)

Summary:
Quick hands-on demo of Redwood's Eval/Console + Optimize flows focused on per-prompt monitoring, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons. Discussed POC plan (1-week, A/B traffic split), compliance touchpoints (SOC 2, KMS), and next steps for trial tenant + prompt upload.

Topics covered: prompt sets, pairwise A/B comparison, regression alerting thresholds, webhook + Slack notifications, private deployment considerations (VPC/KMS), demo of console UI and API sample for evals.

--- Transcript (auto) ---
[00:00:08] Alex (AE): All right, hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro — I'm Alex, AE at Redwood. With me is Priya, our SE who owns the evalops flow.
[00:00:18] Priya (SE): Hi hi. I'll take us through a short demo and then we can jump into the A/B piece.
[00:00:22] Jordan (Customer): Thanks — Jordan here. We're trying to get a sense for how Redwood would catch prompt regressions across different product flows — particularly for our triage assistant and billing assistant prompts.
[00:00:30] Riley (Customer): Yeah, and we want to compare an A/B rollout of a new instruction tuning to see delta on hallucination rates and answer accuracy.
[00:00:36] Dana (Customer): From security I'm mostly interested in what logs are stored and what encryption is used — KMS details, retention.
[00:00:42] Alex: Great, that's exactly what we'll show. Priya, take it away.

[00:01:10] Priya: Ok jumping into the console — first thing is the Prompt Set page, where you can upload CSV or JSONL of prompts. We recommend grouping prompts by user intent and tagging with expected metadata, e.g., "intent:billing". The eval run creates a baseline and stores per-prompt metrics — we compute response-level quality using a configurable scoring suite (we call it "Quality Score", it can be BLEU-like or rubrics).
[00:01:35] Riley: When you say "Quality Score" is that the redwood default or can we plug in an internal metric?
[00:01:40] Priya: You can plug in your own. There are three modes — Redwood native, custom Python scorer via the eval API, or a webhook-based scorer. The webhook option is useful if you already run heavy eval logic internally.
[00:01:52] Jordan: Any latency hit if we use webhook scoring? We need near-realtime alerts.
[00:01:56] Priya: Good question — webhook scoring is async; we run it post-response and ingest the score. For realtime routing you can use an internal fast scorer or the in-console lightweight heuristics. The alerts are driven by stored metrics and will fire as soon as the ingestion pipeline notes a drift beyond threshold.

[00:02:30] [00:02:30] Alex: Quick aside, we also have a continuous baseline option — it rolls the baseline window to the latest N days so your thresholds adapt over time. Helpful to avoid false positives after a model update.

[00:03:05] Priya: Now the A/B comparison flow — you define two variants, e.g., model-v1 on 80% traffic and model-v2 on 20% (or a true 50/50). Redwood collects per-prompt paired samples when possible and runs pairwise statistical tests. We'll show the pairwise UI.
[00:03:22] [00:03:22] (screen share begins)
[00:03:30] Priya: Here's a live A/B run we did internally. You can view aggregated metrics (mean quality score, hallucination rate, avg tokens) and also drill down to the prompt-level view which shows sample outputs side-by-side. Useful for triage.
[00:03:47] Riley: How do you detect hallucination? Is that just a regex or model-based?
[00:03:52] Priya: It's configurable — default uses heuristics plus an optional entailment model. Many customers use a combination: a quick regex-based check for entity mismatch + an entailment scorer for semantic correctness.
[00:04:05] Jordan: Important for us — we need per-customer thresholds and different thresholds per intent.
[00:04:10] Priya: Yep, you can set thresholds per-prompt-tag and per-route. Alerts are evaluated in a rules engine where you can chain conditions: e.g., if hallucination_rate > 3% for billing intents AND quality_score drops by > 10% vs baseline -> trigger P0 alert.
[00:04:28] Dana: Can those alerts be routed to our SRE Slack channel and create PagerDuty incidents?
[00:04:32] Alex: Yes — webhooks, Slack, PagerDuty. Also email or a Jira ticket integration. All alert payloads include sample inputs/outputs, and an obfuscated user id for privacy.

[00:04:58] [00:04:58] (Priya scrolls)
[00:05:04] Priya: Now I'll show the API example — it's a POST to /evals/run with the prompt set id and scorer config. Here's a sample cURL in the chat. You can schedule runs daily or run on-demand.
[00:05:18] Speaker 1: (muffled) Do you support running this in our VPC?
[00:05:22] Priya: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem. In that case, eval ingestion and scoring can remain inside your network and logs can be sent to your KMS/HSM key. There are some bandwidth caveats if you choose on-prem kernels for very large batches.
[00:05:39] Riley: How about data retention? We have to keep only 90 days of PII-free logs.
[00:05:43] Alex: Retention policies are configurable per-tenant. We can TTL artifacts and also redact PII before storage. We'll share the retention config doc.

[00:06:10] Priya: Switching back to the UI — here's the regression alerts tab. You can create a rule that triggers on metric deltas and set a cooldown window. The UI will also show a timeline with when baseline shifted and which deploy caused it (we link to the rollout).
[00:06:28] Jordan: Can we tie a rule to a specific commit or model version?
[00:06:32] Priya: Yes, rollout metadata from the deployment is included in the eval event — model version, container hash, and optional commit link.
[00:06:40] [00:06:40] (minor crosstalk)
[00:06:44] Dana: For compliance — does Redwood keep full example outputs in logs? We prefer storing hashes and minimal text.
[00:06:50] Alex: That's configurable — you can store only hash+metadata, or store outputs encrypted with your KMS and set access controls. If you're on the Private product, the control plane enforces tenant-level RBAC.
[00:07:05] Dana: Ok, please send SOC 2 and any FedRAMP guidance if available.
[00:07:09] Alex: Will do.

[00:07:40] Priya: Back to A/B — here's pairwise comparison for a single prompt. We show the confidence intervals and p-values. If you prefer a more interpretable view, we also do a pairwise majority-vote of human labels (if you upload human evals) and show concordance.
[00:08:00] Riley: Is human labeling integrated? We use a third-party labeling tool.
[00:08:04] Priya: We can ingest human labels via CSV or integrate with common label platforms through webhooks. We also have light-weight crowd microtasks if you need quick checks.

[00:08:30] [00:08:30] Alex: A note on cost — eval runs are priced per sample plus compute for scoring (if you use Redwood scoring). Using your own scorer (webhook) reduces our compute charge. Priya, can you show the cost estimator?
[00:08:45] Priya: Sure — here's the cost estimator in the Optimize tab. You input samples per day, expected sample length, and scoring mode. It suggests batching configs and whether quantized model variants would be cost-effective. For POC we typically run a subset (2k prompts) to keep costs low.
[00:09:06] Jordan: That helps. For the POC, we propose 2k representative prompts across billing and triage.

[00:09:30] Priya: Next, alerts manifest. Demo of an alert card — clicking opens a triage view with examples, delta charts, and a quick rollback to a previous model (one-click fallback).
[00:09:45] Riley: One-click rollback sounds risky — is there a dry-run?
[00:09:50] Priya: Rollback is gated by RBAC and requires an approval step. You can also configure automatic fallback for certain SLO breaches.

[00:10:10] [00:10:10] (screen share shows webhook payload)
[00:10:15] Priya: Here's the webhook payload — it contains metric diffs, sample inputs/outputs (can be redacted), and a trace_id for deeper logs. Many customers wire this into a triage microservice.
[00:10:28] Jordan: We use an internal triage tool; good to know the payload is flexible.

[00:10:55] Alex: Quick performance note — if you run evals against variants on Redwood Dedicated, you get lower latency and consistent throughput; good for high-sample rate POCs. If you need everything inside your network use Private.
[00:11:12] Dana: Do you support bringing your own HSM?
[00:11:15] Alex: Yes for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. We'll include our integration checklist.

[00:11:40] Priya: Now I'll run a short live eval using your example prompt set — small subset we preloaded. This will generate the side-by-side outputs and quality score.
[00:12:02] [00:12:02] (demo run takes ~20s)
[00:12:25] Priya: Run finished — sample prompt: "How do I update my payment method?" Model A answered with the expected steps; Model B added an extra irrelevant suggestion (a hallucination). Quality delta is -12% for Model B.
[00:12:40] Riley: I see the excerpt — can we hide user PII in the sample?
[00:12:44] Priya: We redact common PII patterns automatically and you can add custom redaction rules.

[00:13:20] Jordan: For A/B traffic split — will we get paired samples or independent samples? We need paired to compute per-prompt deltas.
[00:13:27] Priya: If the routing allows us to capture both variants for the same prompt (like shadow traffic), we store paired samples. Otherwise we do statistical tests on independent samples but pairwise is preferred when possible.

[00:13:55] [00:13:55] Alex: Some practical POC notes — we'll provision a trial tenant, you upload the canonical prompt set, tag by intent, and we'll run nightly evals and enable regression alerts. Priya will instrument webhooks to your triage.
[00:14:12] Jordan: Sounds good. How long to get trial tenant?
[00:14:16] Priya: We can spin one up in 24 hours once we have the prompt set and account owner.

[00:14:45] Dana: One more compliance Q — does Redwood support SAML SSO for console access?
[00:14:49] Alex: Yes SAML and SCIM for user provisioning. For Private there is more control over identity providers.

[00:15:10] [00:15:10] (brief hold while Priya shares doc link)
[00:15:18] Priya: Dropping links: sample eval runbook (link), POC SOW template (link), SOC2 summary (link).
[00:15:30] Riley: Thanks.

[00:15:55] Jordan: Ok breaking away to internal priorities — what would success look like for the POC? We'd want to see a measurable reduction in hallucination by at least 30% or a clear detection with alerts within 1 hour of a bad rollout.
[00:16:10] Priya: We can validate both. For the alerting latency, we'll set ingestion and alerting cadence to near realtime for the POC. For detection threshold we'll tune per-intent.

[00:16:40] Alex: Anything else we didn't cover?
[00:16:44] Dana: Please also document the data flows — who's processing what when on a Private deployment.
[00:16:48] Alex: Noted. We'll include the data flow diagram.

[00:17:10] [00:17:10] (wrapping up)
[00:17:15] Priya: Quick recap of next steps: we'll provision trial tenant, upload the 2k prompt subset, enable A/B with a 20% variant, wire webhooks to your triage, and share SOC2 + KMS checklist.
[00:17:28] Alex: I'll follow up with pricing and the SOW. Jordan, Dana — anything else?
[00:17:33] Jordan: No, thanks. Excited to see it in action.
[00:17:36] Dana: Please include retention configuration options in the follow up.
[00:17:39] Alex: Will do.

[00:18:00] (meeting continues with light Q&A; remainder are clarifications and scheduling)
[00:32:20] [00:32:20] Riley: One oddity — in the pairwise view we saw a false-positive on a non-deterministic prompt. How do we handle variance?
[00:32:29] Priya: We use sample bucketing and randomized seeds for deterministic comparisons during the POC; we also recommend a longer baseline window for high-variance prompts.

[00:36:50] [00:36:50] Jordan: Can Redwood surface which exact prompt led to a regression in the rollout UI?
[00:36:55] Priya: Yes — the impact heatmap highlights top N prompts contributing to the aggregate delta and you can filter by intent, route, or user cohort.

[00:41:05] [00:41:05] Alex: Ok final administrative notes — we'll set up a follow-up call next Tuesday to review the initial POC results.
[00:41:12] Jordan: Sounds good.

[00:46:58] (meeting ends at ~15:47 PST; recording clipped a few seconds)

End of transcript.
